high.title: Ringgit strengthens ahead of US Fed rate decision
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0835/4.0875 against the US dollar as investors awaited the critical FOMC meeting on July 28-29. Falling crude oil prices due to easing US-Iran tensions also influenced currency movements. The Fed's rate decision will have direct implications for ringgit direction and Malaysian capital flows.

high.title: Bursa ends higher on bargain hunting
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia rebounded as easing West Asia tensions drove Brent crude down nearly 8%, improving investor sentiment across regional markets. Analysts maintain a cautious near-term outlook ahead of the US Fed policy decision and major tech earnings. The rotation back into risk assets signals renewed but selective investor confidence in Malaysian equities.

high.title: Oil prices sink as US-Iran pause fuels fresh Hormuz hopes
high.summary: A ceasefire pause between the US and Iran triggered a sharp drop in oil prices after Brent had broken above US$100 per barrel, its highest since May. Easing tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea shipping lanes are critical for global energy supply stability. For Malaysia, an oil-dependent economy, this shift significantly impacts Petronas revenues, the ringgit, and the national budget outlook.

high.title: Bursa Retreats as Market Digests Latest US Tariffs
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia declined as the US imposed new tariffs and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pushed Brent crude above US$100 per barrel before easing. The FBM KLCI faced selling pressure though outperformed regional peers, with the 1,700 level seen as a key technical support. Escalating West Asia supply risks and inflation concerns are weighing heavily on global and local market sentiment.

high.title: Ringgit Ends Slightly Lower Amid Middle East Tensions, US Tariffs
high.summary: The ringgit weakened amid a confluence of pressures including a new 10% US forced labour-related tariff on Malaysian exports that took effect on July 24 and rising crude oil prices driven by the Strait of Hormuz blockade. MITI confirmed engagement with the US over the tariff, which replaces a temporary measure under Section 122 of the Trade Act 1974. These external risks are elevating demand for the US dollar and threatening global supply chains.

high.title: Ringgit Rises Against US Dollar Ahead of Negeri Sembilan Poll
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened slightly to 4.0830/4.0930 against the US dollar as markets await the outcome of the Negeri Sembilan state election and the critical FOMC meeting on July 28-29. Analysts warn that the increasing likelihood of a US rate hike could boost the dollar and pressure the ringgit. Both domestic political developments and external monetary policy signals are key near-term drivers for the currency.

high.title: Bursa Opens Lower Amid Cautious Market Sentiment
high.summary: The FBM KLCI fell 6.09 points to 1,708.50 in early trading as Brent crude surpassed US$100 per barrel and Wall Street's Nasdaq dropped 2.15% following negative reactions to Alphabet's and Tesla's spending plans. Losers outpaced gainers 336 to 151, signalling broad-based selling pressure. This combination of elevated oil prices and tech sector weakness poses significant headwinds for Malaysian equities.

high.title: Ringgit Opens Higher Against Major Currencies, Softer vs US Dollar
high.summary: The ringgit softened against the US dollar to 4.0925/4.0980 after Trump announced additional import tariffs of 10%–12.5% on 60 economies including Malaysia, citing forced labour practices. This marks a renewed trade policy threat that could directly impact Malaysian exports and business sentiment. The ringgit is expected to trade cautiously in the RM4.08–RM4.10 range.

high.title: Ringgit Ends Lower Amid Middle East Tensions
high.summary: The ringgit eased to 4.0870/4.0910 against the US dollar as surging crude oil prices — WTI up 3.19% and Brent up 4.23% — driven by re-escalating Middle East conflicts raised global inflation concerns. The possibility of a US interest rate hike in September strengthened the US dollar, putting further pressure on the ringgit. This oil price shock has broad implications for Malaysia's monetary policy and import costs.

high.title: Ringgit ends higher against US dollar, other currencies amid rising oil prices
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened as Brent crude surged above US$94 per barrel, with Malaysia benefiting as an energy exporter generating an additional RM300 million in government revenue per US$1 oil price increase. However, market sentiment remained cautious due to disruptions in key Middle East shipping straits and new US tariff measures on generic drugs. These factors have significant implications for Malaysia's fiscal position and trade outlook.

high.title: Ringgit eases against US dollar, tracks major currencies
high.summary: The ringgit edged slightly lower at 4.0855/4.0920 against the US dollar as odds for a US Fed rate hike in September rose to 64.8%, signalling near-term dollar strength. Despite this, the ringgit showed resilience supported by strong Malaysian trade data and its status as an energy exporter amid rising oil prices. The potential Fed rate hike represents a critical external risk factor for Malaysian currency and capital flows.

high.title: Bursa ends lower amid profit-taking, higher oil prices
high.summary: The FBM KLCI fell 0.52% to 1,711.37 as profit-taking and elevated crude oil prices dampened risk appetite amid escalating Middle East tensions involving Houthi threats to regional shipping. Analysts view the pullback as a healthy consolidation following a strong rally from around 1,655, with bargain-hunting opportunities emerging in fundamentally sound large-cap stocks. Continued foreign fund inflows and resilient domestic fundamentals are expected to underpin the broader market recovery.

medium.title: Bursa rebounds at open as investors track pause in US airstrikes
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose at market open, gaining 2.05 points to 1,703.07, as easing geopolitical tensions and softer energy prices encouraged buying after last week's sell-off. Gainers outpaced losers in early trade, suggesting broad-based but cautious recovery. Malaysian investors are closely watching the US Fed decision and Big Tech earnings as near-term market catalysts.

medium.title: German sports carmaker Porsche to cut 5,000 jobs by 2035
medium.summary: Porsche announced a plan to reduce its workforce by 8,900 people by 2035 amid collapsing profits driven by weak China sales, US tariffs, and a costly EV transition. The company will invest €2.1 billion in two German plants while implementing voluntary and attrition-based job reductions. This reflects broader global auto industry pressures from Chinese EV competition, relevant to Malaysian automotive sector investors and EV policy watchers.

medium.title: Westports Outperforms Despite Middle East Fallout
medium.summary: Westports posted a strong Q2 FY2026 net profit jump of 56% to RM360.9 million and H1 revenue rose 34% to RM1.76 billion, beating analyst expectations despite a 40% surge in fuel costs. Container volume dipped 1% in H1, but profitability held up well amid the Middle East conflict disruptions. Multiple research houses maintained 'buy' calls, signalling continued investor confidence in the port operator.

medium.title: Khazanah Said to Sell US$340mil Tenaga Stake in Placement
medium.summary: Khazanah Nasional reportedly sold 100 million Tenaga Nasional shares at RM13.91 each, representing a 4.5% discount to the market price, in a confidential block placement worth approximately US$340 million. The sale reduces Khazanah's stake in Tenaga, one of Malaysia's largest listed utilities. This significant divestment could signal portfolio rebalancing by the sovereign wealth fund and may affect Tenaga's share price and shareholder structure.

medium.title: Bursa Snaps 3-Day Losing Streak to End Higher
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 3.22 points to 1,714.59, ending a three-day losing streak as buying interest in oil and gas and utilities stocks offset weakness in large-cap counters. Turnover narrowed to RM2.27 billion from RM2.50 billion the previous day, suggesting selective but cautious recovery. The rebound in O&G stocks reflects investor positioning amid rising crude oil prices.

medium.title: Bursa Opens Higher on Global Tech Earnings Spillover
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI gained 3.42 points at opening to 1,714.79, buoyed by positive spillover from Alphabet's stronger-than-expected Q2 FY2026 results driven by Google Cloud growth. Gainers outpaced losers 203 to 134 in early trade, reflecting improved risk appetite. The tech earnings optimism provided temporary support for Bursa before broader global headwinds took hold later in the day.

medium.title: Blackstone lines up US$3bil AirTrunk loan as data centre debt concerns grow
medium.summary: Blackstone is securing a US$3 billion loan from a consortium of major banks including DBS and UOB to fund AirTrunk's SYD3 hyperscale data centre, highlighting growing regional data centre investment activity relevant to Malaysian investors in the tech and REIT sectors. The deal underscores surging AI infrastructure financing, with over US$334.5 billion raised globally in 2026 alone, far exceeding 2025 totals. Malaysian-linked banks and data centre operators may see spillover opportunities and risks from this rapidly expanding debt market.
